geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the single bent bar with a split-wing massing to open a clearer ground void and create a stronger public threshold while preserving the dominant anchor.
Keep the dominant separation organized along the main section axis so the mass remains one coherent gesture.
Introduce a meaningful gap that can register as public void rather than decorative cut.
Preserve a continuous ground anchor so the new void reads as an entry/court condition rather than two disconnected fragments.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant massing idea from a mostly sealed court block to a clearer carved figure that can produce a legible public ground response.
Increase the carved void so it reads as an actual usable court rather than a token subtraction.
Align the public opening to the verified access side in the program frame so the frontage becomes legible.
Lower the terrace link to strengthen the active ground threshold and make the entry/void more consequential.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant bent/prismatic mass across all four views, so gesture clarity is decent and it is not visually fragmented. However, the form is primarily a compact block with a slight bend and a clipped top; the internal logic does not produce a convincing public void or active ground threshold on the verified access edge. The blue frontage is met by a mostly sealed face, so the access response is semantically weak for neighborhood living. The silhouette is coherent but only modestly resolved as a massing section, because the stepping/clipping does not yet carry a clear inhabited terrace or daylight/entry consequence. The mass can plausibly hold the program in broad terms, but the visible ground-to-upper hierarchy and public-space logic are underdeveloped. It resembles a mixed-use prism more than a neighborhood living building with an active edge and one legible terrace/court.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More tower-prism than low-rise neighborhood living; exterior expression is not directly transferable as a massing solution.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact prismatic mixed-use mass with a clear dominant object and legible carved relationship to the ground.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Primarily a different program and spatial scale; do not copy the garden-like atmosphere as building form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong edge condition and a sheltered, courtyard-like public realm can support a social ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Restaurant-specific enclosure and intimacy dominate; use only the void/threshold idea.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A calm mass can still organize an inviting public-to-private transition through enclosed outdoor room logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tall office-tower typology is not program-equivalent and would overstate verticality here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A stacked or stepped upper mass can coexist with a more active lower zone if the ground remains differentiated.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual typology; too infrastructural and too slender to serve as the dominant neighborhood-living mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A bridge-like figure can suggest porous circulation and public movement across a site.

warnings: Blue access edge is not clearly answered by a public void, seam, or entry carve.
Open-space figure is too small/ambiguous to read as usable public space.
The form remains slightly box-like despite the bent operation.
Do not overinterpret the top clip as a meaningful program section.
